description: A real case that is neither AO-26005B's order nor PO5447, picked at run time from live data and opened through the generic tools (GET only). One host capture cycle (operating.host: the sales- and purchase-order Portal relations into the source mirror, the BC sales invoices of every pinned company into the BC capture), then offline over those captures: pick=SalesInvoice>SalesOrder (a join pick, operating.case_workspace_live.join_carriers: the newest BC sales invoice whose carried identifier, as the schema's cross-system SalesInvoice.bills bindings declare it (externalDocumentNumber as the Portal order number, its earlier numbers, or the customer's PO, which the Portal sends as the BC order's externalDocumentNumber), or as a declared path of two hops with one between the systems carries it (its BC orderNumber to the Portal order renumbered to it, SalesInvoice.bills > SalesOrder.same_record_as renumberedTo, or to the order whose own number BC kept, order_number, the two hops' kinds bc_document_no and so_number declared aliases of one another in the identifier registry, a lead (plx-customer-portal@340ef1e portal/src/lib/business-central/align-portal-so-number.ts); its shipment code to that Portal shipment's order: SalesInvoice.for_shipment > Shipment.ships, plx-customer-portal@d52c32c document-finance-queries.ts:47-123), plx.find resolves to exactly one Portal sales order, a customer PO only when that order's customer is the same record as the invoice's (the Portal's customer + PO match); that order roots the case and the invoice is cited beside it) and pick=PurchaseOrder+ReceiptLine (the newest Portal PO with a received line). Every newer invoice that joined no Portal order gets one typed reason (JOIN_REASONS: no_portal_row_for_external_document_number, not_in_served_replica for an environment-prefixed reference such as UAT-, portal_row_unreadable_for_reader, portal_carrier_unread, find_live_error, ambiguous_root, scope_mismatch (the PO's order belongs to another customer), cross_scope (a BC record of another BC company holds the same number: BC numbers are unique only within a company, so the match is never joined), scope_unread (either customer not shown as one record at a verified or reviewed tier: a lead link, such as a Portal customer's erp_code on a BC number of no known company, never joins), identity_lead_only, normalized_only, path_unreached (a two-hop path's matched record reaches no one order), no_identifier, root_not_readable), and every scanned invoice one outcome per carrier (joined or its reason, keyed by the carrier's target binding and field, a two-hop path's cross-system one), counted per case (cases[*].pick) and in pick_root_reasons / pick_carrier_outcomes; the reasons are recorded on the opened case as one pick_unjoined gap. The check passes only with a cited cross-rooted case (json_min cited_cross_rooted 1): while BC documents name Portal rows the served replica never holds (the UAT drain), red with the reason counts is the truthful state. Counts and enums only, never an identifier or value.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check runs it; module tests are injected-transport (operating/tests/test_unfamiliar_order_case.py: the spec's own command over an in-process FakeWorkbench and FakeBc, its expectations checked on the real summary, and a Portal answering HTTP 500 at capture meeting expect_blocked). Replaces the retired operating.order_case_script command (task allowlist-3); the root reasons it recorded survive here as the join pick's typed reasons (the retired command's last live record, per the acceptance: no_portal_row_for_external_document_number 37 of 40 BC roots, 35 of them renumbered_suspect, i.e. not SO-number shaped; not re-measured here). Since the customer-PO carrier (task invoice-join-customer-po-carrier) a PO-carried invoice joins its customer's order or names scope_mismatch / scope_unread; since task scope-party-identity-tiers only a verified or reviewed same_record_as (ontology_tools.same_party) joins the two customers, so roots lost to lead-only customer links are counted as scope_unread in pick_root_reasons; renumbered_suspect is replaced by the per-carrier outcomes. Daily: the old check ran 1352 s; one host cycle of 16 relations and the BC sales invoices of three companies, one projection and two cases share the 2400 s timeout (seconds.capture/open/render are recorded so the first run measures it). Since task bc-invoice-join-paths (13 red verdicts, the last pick 47 no_portal_row_for_external_document_number and 3 not_in_served_replica of 50, only the direct carrier tried) the two declared two-hop paths are tried too, a prefixed reference is not_in_served_replica for its own carriers only, and a match only roots at its carrier's declared field; whether live invoices join through them is unmeasured until the next daily. Since task unfamiliar-order-pick-intersect a pick whose newest PICK_SCAN invoices join nothing turns around: the Portal orders whose numbers (order_number, fmOeNumber, erpCode, renumberedTo, po_reference) a held BC invoice carries, intersected over the whole projection, propose up to PICK_SCAN more invoices, each decided by the same join through the tools; pick_directions (and cases[*].pick.directions) count each direction: forward.scanned/joined, reverse.start_held (invoices carrying a joinable value), linked_held (Portal orders carrying one), linked_matched (under the relation grants, before any per-row rule), scanned, joined and reasons, order-number twins proposed before customer-PO ones. The live run of 2026-10-16 (candidate da08575a8) showed why that alone cannot join: the BC capture held 2 invoices (both UAT-prefixed: not_in_served_replica 2) against 800 Portal orders. So the reverse direction then asks BC itself, GET only through the live BC reader (ontology.resolve.BcLookup over the host config's bc.books when it names one, else the default integrations/bc_company_books.json; the live-check host config names none, so the default list is used; the live audience gating each read): for the newest Portal orders the investigator reads (at most PICK_SCAN), one $filter equality per carried order number and pinned company (never a prefixed value, never a customer PO), each invoice found decided by the same join (one number in two BC companies, or a company read cut short: cross_scope), the joined one cited live beside the root as a lead. pick_directions.reverse.bc counts reader (cases with a live BC reader), orders, orders_unreadable, requests (BC GETs sent), lookups (company units BC answered: read, truncated or unreadable; never one withheld, unpinned or not searchable), lookup_states (every probe per state), hits and scanned; a company outside the books, or one unread or cut short, leaves the number cross_scope. The live run of 73775fc89 timed out at 40 min with no output: the forward direction's plx.find fell through to unbounded live BC probes per root (about 37 min). Both directions now share one wall clock per pick, PICK_BUDGET_SECONDS (420 s; integrations.live_source_guard.RequestDeadline: every live request checked against it before I/O and given at most the time left), and the whole live investigation of each opened case one of OPEN_LIVE_SECONDS (600 s); forward.budget_spent and reverse.budget_spent count the directions cut; a pick cut before anything joined fails as pick_budget_spent, never pick_none_found, and the command still prints its counts. The run of 4130ffdf7 then ended (open 506 s) but spent the whole 420 s on 11 forward roots, about 38 s each (no_portal_row_for_external_document_number 6, not_in_served_replica 3, identity_lead_only 2), so the reverse direction never ran. Now the forward direction spends at most FORWARD_SHARE (half) of the clock and the reverse one always gets the rest (it is not run only once the whole clock has passed), and a join's plx.find the projection cannot answer asks live only the carriers' target families (ontology.resolve.only_sources: the Portal for a Portal order), so a forward root no longer probes every pinned BC company for the invoice it started from; only a live Portal match a company-scoped carrier could root on repeats the find over BC, to keep cross_scope. Roots and carriers the old BC probes made identity_lead_only (a BC record, never a Portal row) may now count their no-Portal-row reason instead. The reverse direction is not run while the Portal could not be read. Counts only; whether the newest live Portal orders have BC invoices is unmeasured until the next daily. Since task unfamiliar-order-replica-blocked the five join changes (bc-invoice-join-paths, bc-invoice-own-number-join, unfamiliar-order-pick-intersect, reverse-pick-through-find, projection-sqlite-full) moved nothing because BC Production drains from plx-postgres-uat while the reporting API serves the plx-postgres-staging replica (later_ask workbench-api-replica-target; the customer PO, environment-independent, got no_portal_row too: externalDocumentNumber 47/50, reverse hits 0, linked_matched 0 of 800). When the pick ran both directions to the end (no budget_spent, a live BC reader, the Portal read, neither type's capture unfinished, nothing refused) and joined nothing, and every root reason is no_portal_row_* or not_in_served_replica with reverse hits 0 and linked_matched 0, the summary sets pick_blocked (not_in_served_replica) and that case is blocked, not failed: the check reads blocked, cause source_gap (the reuse of case.rec10_external_doc's blocked_when path), citing workbench-api-replica-target; any other reason mix (scope_mismatch, scope_unread, find_live_error ...), a cut clock or an unfinished capture still fails, and the pick-cause order stays refused, unfinished, unjoined (docs/decisions/2026-10-19-pick-cause-mail-unfinished.md). pick_date_months records counts only (type -> YYYY-MM -> held objects by latest event, all held rather than only the scanned) so a time-window mismatch reads apart from an environment mismatch. Live-unverified until the next daily.
